regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unimpeachable until you notice the RBI's own forecast sits at 6.7% YoY — a 110bps gap that historically reflects deflator assumptions, not output. PMI Composite at 55.9 and IIP at 8.0% YoY corroborate momentum, but core sector at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%) is the goods economy's honest confession. Capacity utilisation crossing 77.4% of capacity for the first time in 18 months is the one number that makes the growth story structurally credible — it means the next capex wave has a demand foundation, not just a policy nudge.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is already above the RBI's 5.1% YoY forecast, and the decomposition is unflattering: food at 7.74% YoY rising for two consecutive months, fuel at 22.93% YoY at a 10-year high, and WPI at 9.92% YoY signalling that producer prices will feed into consumer prices with a one-to-two quarter lag. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is the one comfort — but invert it: if core stays contained while fuel and food surge, the RBI faces a political economy problem, not a monetary one. Cutting into a 22.93% fuel print would be indefensible; holding means real rates stay positive and the capex IRR calculus tightens.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY sounds manageable until you note that corporate bond issuance sits at ₹18,700 cr / month — the 4th percentile historically — meaning the wholesale funding market is not absorbing the slack. CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits has eased from 83% but remains at the 71st percentile; the last time it sustained here was FY14, and the taper tantrum forced an emergency 75bps reversal within 12 months. NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY rising for two consecutive months while their bond issuance window is effectively closed is the stress fracture the regulator is watching.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged and the RBI's communiqué signals no near-term move — but the data is making that stance increasingly uncomfortable. Real repo rate against headline CPI of 5.54% YoY is effectively negative 29bps; against the RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY it is barely positive. With US 10Y at 5.1% yield and the INR at 94.34, the RBI cannot cut without triggering FII outflows that dwarf DII absorption capacity. The policy rate is frozen not by conviction but by the geometry of the external account.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY accelerating from 16.1% YoY, combined with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — first print above 77% in 18 months — is the most credible capex signal in two years. Bank credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and services at 24.3% YoY rising for two consecutive months confirms that credit is chasing real investment demand, not financial engineering. The one inversion worth stating: core sector at 4.8% YoY, which measures actual physical throughput of cement, steel, and electricity, is decelerating — if it doesn't recover within two quarters, the IIP capex goods number is measuring orders, not delivery.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month at the 74th percentile is solid but not accelerating — the month-on-month move from ₹1,99,853 cr is modest and the FYTD at ₹12,46,000 cr sits at only the 25th percentile, suggesting base effects are flattering the headline. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY falling for two consecutive months (from 26.1%) is the urban discretionary warning; two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounding sharply is the rural demand signal that contradicts it. The divergence — mass-market rural recovery, premium urban deceleration — is exactly what you'd expect when fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY compresses urban disposable income faster than rural wage growth.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit +19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposits +17.8% YoY — a 160bps divergence that has widened for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit, 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 71st percentile historically. NBFC credit +15.8% YoY, rising 2 in a row. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month — 4th percentile, a warning sign of wholesale funding stress.","implication":"Banks are lending faster than they can gather deposits. This forces two outcomes: (1) RBI will face pressure to cut rates to ease deposit competition, despite inflation at 5.54% YoY; (2) NBFCs and smaller banks with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities face margin compression and refinancing risk. Overweight private banks with CASA >45% (they poach deposits). Underweight NBFC bonds with maturity <2 years. Watch for RBI to signal rate cuts in next policy review.","pct_10y":71,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 71st percentile is elevated but not extreme. Historically, ratios >85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19) and forced RBI to inject liquidity. Current 81% is a yellow flag, not red.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Accelerating Into Q4","data_text":"IIP capital goods +16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% — 53rd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity, up from 75.6%, at 68th percentile — first time above 77% in 18 months. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5%), but this is noise; the capex signal is in capgoods and utilisation. India credit to industry +18.2% YoY, services +24.3% YoY (rising 2 in a row) — both tracking capex-led demand.","implication":"Capacity utilisation >77% is the trigger for private capex. Expect Q4 FY26 and FY27 to see accelerated capex announcements in cement, steel, auto, and infra. Overweight capital goods suppliers (Cummins, Escorts, Bharat Electronics). Overweight cement (Ultratech, Ambuja) — utilisation gains flow to pricing power. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex cycle crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 68th percentile — the sweet spot where firms shift from cost-cutting to expansion. This preceded the 2014-16 capex cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 95th Percentile, But Growth Slowing","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest), rising 3 in a row (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490). At 95th percentile historically. But SIP YoY growth at 10.7%, down from 15% three months ago — a 420bps deceleration. SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (latest), down from 10.45 mn — accounts shrinking while AUM grows. SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr, up 2 of last 3. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month, up from ₹29,329 cr — 85th percentile.","implication":"SIP flows are at record nominal levels but growth is decelerating — classic late-cycle behaviour. The divergence between rising AUM and falling account count means average ticket size is rising; affluent money is entering, not mass retail. This is a warning: retail participation is narrowing. Reduce equity MF allocations. Rotate from small/mid-cap (retail-driven) to large-cap (institutional-driven). Watch for SIP growth to turn negative in next 2 months — that's your exit signal.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 95th percentile are historically associated with market peaks (2021, 2024). Growth deceleration from 15% to 10.7% preceded corrections in both instances.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile — Demand Shock Risk","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% — at 95th percentile, the highest in 10 years. Brent crude at $96.08/bbl (latest), up from $92.18/bbl three months ago. WTI at $88.92/bbl. Natural gas at $3.242/MMBtu, up from $3.21/MMBtu. FAO food index at 136 index, up from 130.3 — 63rd percentile. India's headline CPI at 5.54% YoY, food at 7.74% YoY (rising 2 in a row).","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile will force RBI to hold rates higher for longer, despite deposit stress. This kills the rate-cut narrative. Oil >$95/bbl is a demand shock — either global growth is accelerating (bullish) or geopolitical risk is rising (bearish). Given China PMI at 52.1 (neutral) and US PMI at 58.4 (strong), the risk is geopolitical. Hedge with long oil, short INR. Avoid airlines (margin compression) and auto (fuel cost pass-through limited). Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) — they benefit from higher crude.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile preceded the 2022 rate hike cycle and the 2008 demand shock. Current level is unsustainable without demand destruction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Breaks Carry Trade Funding","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (latest), up from 1% — at 100th percentile, the highest in 10 years. Rising 2 in a row. Fed funds at 3.88% p.a., up from 3.75%, at 75th percentile. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a., up from 2.25%. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (80th percentile), China PMI at 52.1 (54th percentile).","implication":"BOJ tightening at 100th percentile is breaking the yen carry trade — the funding mechanism for global risk assets. Higher US Treasury yields (93rd percentile) are competing with equities. The divergence between strong US growth (PMI 58.4) and weak China (PMI 52.1) means capital is rotating from EM to US. FII flows to India are negative (₹-49,935 cr / month net), at 14th percentile. Reduce India equity exposure. Rotate to US large-cap (S&P 500 at 100th percentile). Hedge INR weakness — it will accelerate as carry unwinds.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile is a regime break. The last time BOJ was this tight (2018), EM currencies crashed and risk assets sold off 15-20%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening Into 94.34 — RBI Defending Quietly","data_text":"INR/USD at 94.34 ₹ (latest), up from 93.46 ₹ three months ago — at 89th percentile, near 10-year highs. Weakening 2 of last 5 periods. FII equity net flows at ₹-49,935 cr / month (latest), at 14th percentile — massive outflows. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (96th percentile) — domestic money is the only bid. India household debt at 47.8% of GDP, up from 47.1%, at 60th percentile. Corporate debt at 54.5% of GDP, up from 53.9%.","implication":"INR is weakening because FIIs are exiting (carry trade unwind + US rate premium). This kills the rate-cut narrative and pressures consumption (higher import costs). Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto components) — they benefit from INR weakness. Underweight importers and consumption plays. Build a long INR position for a 2-3 month horizon — RBI will defend at 95.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile is near the 2022 crisis level (95.5). RBI has ₹600bn in FX reserves — enough to defend for 3-4 months if outflows persist.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapsed — GCC Rotation Underway","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 19.5 mn sq ft three quarters ago — a 79% collapse. At -100 percentile (worst in 10 years). Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant, down from 14.5%, but this is misleading — the vacancy decline is due to supply destruction, not demand. Nifty IT at flat (no upside despite office collapse). But Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are absorbing 40-50% of new office space in Bangalore and Hyderabad (not captured in traditional IT metrics). Rent in Bangalore at ₹103.6/sqft/mo (down from ₹168.8/sqft/mo), Hyderabad at ₹103.52 index (up from 99.87) — GCCs are moving to Tier-2 cities for cost arbitrage. Airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month (32nd percentile) — business travel is NOT recovering despite office absorption collapse.","implication":"Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are losing office space to GCCs (captive centres of MNCs). This is a structural shift: IT services are commoditising, GCCs are capturing high-margin work. The Nifty IT index is a value trap — it's not recovering because the business model is broken. Underweight IT services. Overweight IT infrastructure plays (data centres, office REITs in Tier-2 cities). The real signal: business travel is dead (86.4 mn pax at 32nd percentile), so office-dependent models (consulting, IT services) are structurally impaired. Rotate to software (SaaS, AI), not services.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at -100 percentile is a regime break. The last time absorption was this low (2020 COVID), it preceded a 3-year structural decline in office demand. GCC rotation is the new normal.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline, 4.8% Core Sector — Two Economies, One Number

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY accelerated from 7.4% YoY; PMI Composite at 55.9 (59th percentile) and IIP at 8.0% YoY corroborate the expansion.
  • But core sector at 4.8% YoY — the physical throughput of cement, steel, electricity, and coal — decelerated from 5.0% YoY, the goods economy's honest counter-signal.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (68th percentile) crossed above 77% for the first time in 18 months — the threshold at which private capex historically accelerates without policy subsidy.
  • RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% YoY vs the headline 7.8% YoY — a 110bps gap that reflects deflator assumptions and statistical discrepancy, not a genuine output divergence the market should dismiss.

The tension: The headline GDP and PMI signal an economy firing on all cylinders; core sector deceleration and the RBI's own 110bps-lower forecast suggest the quality of growth is thinner than the number implies.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a third consecutive month below 5.0% YoY would signal that the capex upcycle is generating orders but not yet physical output.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 5.1% — The Rate That Reprices Everything Else

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.1% yield (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive sessions — the level at which EM carry trades historically unwind and dollar funding costs bite.
  • Fed Funds at 3.88% p.a. (75th percentile) rising for three consecutive periods; US GDP SAAR at 3.4% SAAR — the Fed has no political cover to pause tightening.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, a 10-year high) rising for two consecutive periods — yen carry unwind is compressing global liquidity simultaneously with the US tightening.
  • But US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at a 10-year-high suggest equity markets are not yet pricing the rate reality that bond markets are screaming.

The tension: Bond markets are pricing a sustained high-rate regime; equity markets in the US and Europe are pricing re-acceleration. One of them is wrong, and the 5.1% US 10Y yield is the mechanism that will force the reconciliation.

Bottom line: If US 10Y sustains above 5.1% yield through next week's Fed commentary, expect FII equity outflows from India to accelerate beyond the current ₹49,935 cr net / month.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII Absorbs FII Exit — But the Fuel Tank Has a Gauge

The facts:

  • FII equity net at ₹-49,935 cr net / month (14th percentile) — the largest outflow in recent memory, driven by US 10Y repricing and INR at 94.34 ₹ (89th percentile).
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr net / month (96th percentile) is the only bid — domestic money is absorbing every rupee of foreign selling, but this is not a structural floor, it is a flow coincidence.
  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (95th percentile) rising for three consecutive months, but SIP YoY growth at 10.7% YoY — down from 15.0% three months ago, a 420bps deceleration.
  • But NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (6th percentile) signal that institutional conviction in deploying fresh capital is near a 10-year low — the pipeline is thinning even as the SIP tap runs.

The tension: SIP autopilot is keeping DII flows elevated, but decelerating SIP growth and near-zero NFO collections mean the domestic absorption capacity is a lagging indicator, not a leading one — it reflects past commitments, not fresh conviction.

Bottom line: Watch SIP YoY growth: a print below 10.0% YoY would signal that the retail bid is structurally narrowing and DII cannot indefinitely offset FII outflows at current magnitudes.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Price Office Collapse; Residential Splits by City and Ticket

The facts:

  • NRI residential buying is FALLING — NRI share at 18% of purchases (prior 15%, but down 2pp vs the earlier print); NRI share within premium/luxury at 32% — the segment most exposed to INR depreciation and global rate tightening.
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, unsold inventory at 28 months — the launch surge is running well ahead of absorption and will pressure prices within 4–6 quarters.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (worst in 10 years) masks a GCC rotation: GCCs now take 42% of new space in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, while traditional IT at 22% shrinks.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down 10–18% from prior prints — the market is pricing IT-services vacancy, not GCC demand.

The tension: REIT unit prices are collapsing on IT-sector optics while GCCs — the actual growth occupier — are expanding aggressively and moving to Tier-2 cities for cost arbitrage; the market is pricing the wrong tenant.

Bottom line: REITs are a mispriced GCC play: Embassy and Mindspace are worth revisiting on a 12-month view if GCC absorption sustains above 40% of new leasing for two consecutive quarters.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Five Fracture Points, Ranked by Probability × Impact

The facts:

  • US 10Y at 5.1% yield (93rd percentile) sustaining — every 25bps above 5.0% compresses India's rate differential, accelerates FII outflows, and forces the RBI to defend INR rather than manage growth. Highest probability × impact.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $96.08/bbl — every $10/bbl adds ~$15bn to India's annual import bill, widens CAD by ~40bps, and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (4th percentile) — if wholesale funding remains this thin, NBFC credit growth at 15.8% YoY becomes unsustainable within two quarters and triggers a risk-weight tightening cycle.
  • INR at 94.34 ₹ (89th percentile) with FII outflows at ₹49,935 cr net / month — RBI defending quietly means reserve drawdown; $680bn in reserves buys time but not indefinitely if BOJ tightening accelerates yen carry unwind.
  • Hyderabad residential launches at +120% YoY against 28 months of unsold inventory — a supply glut in the market with the highest momentum is the real estate risk that no one is discussing yet.

The tension: The external risks (US 10Y, BOJ, INR) and the domestic funding risks (corporate bond market, NBFC stress) are reinforcing each other — a global rate shock tightens the very wholesale funding window that NBFCs need to roll their liabilities.

Bottom line: Watch US 10Y yield: a sustained close above 5.25% yield this week would force an emergency RBI liquidity response and reprice Nifty Bank's earnings trajectory.

"}
